statement: For a rod label d in {0,1,...,9}, say d is complete in rings if for each color byte c in {82 ('R'), 71 ('G'), 66 ('B')} there exists an index j with 0 <= j < n such that rings[2*j] = c and rings[2*j+1] = 48+d. The function returns a result r and r equals the number of rod labels d in {0,1,...,9} that are complete in rings.
preconditions: Let n = len(rings)/2. The byte slice rings has length 2*n for some integer n with 1 <= n <= 100. For every j with 0 <= j < n, rings[2*j] is one of the ASCII bytes 82 ('R'), 71 ('G'), 66 ('B'), and rings[2*j+1] is one of the ASCII bytes 48 ('0') through 57 ('9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= 10.
preconditions: Let n = len(rings)/2. The byte slice rings has length 2*n for some integer n with 1 <= n <= 100. For every j with 0 <= j < n, rings[2*j] is one of the ASCII bytes 82 ('R'), 71 ('G'), 66 ('B'), and rings[2*j+1] is one of the ASCII bytes 48 ('0') through 57 ('9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= U, where U is the number of rod labels d in {0,1,...,9} for which there exists j with 0 <= j < n and rings[2*j+1] = 48+d (that is, U is the number of distinct rod labels occurring in rings).
preconditions: Let n = len(rings)/2. The byte slice rings has length 2*n for some integer n with 1 <= n <= 100. For every j with 0 <= j < n, rings[2*j] is one of the ASCII bytes 82 ('R'), 71 ('G'), 66 ('B'), and rings[2*j+1] is one of the ASCII bytes 48 ('0') through 57 ('9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if no rod label d in {0,1,...,9} is complete in rings; here d is complete exactly when each of the color bytes 82, 71, 66 occurs on rod d, i.e. for each such c there is j with 0 <= j < n, rings[2*j] = c, and rings[2*j+1] = 48+d.
preconditions: Let n = len(rings)/2. The byte slice rings has length 2*n for some integer n with 1 <= n <= 100. For every j with 0 <= j < n, rings[2*j] is one of the ASCII bytes 82 ('R'), 71 ('G'), 66 ('B'), and rings[2*j+1] is one of the ASCII bytes 48 ('0') through 57 ('9').

statement: If at least one of the color bytes 82 ('R'), 71 ('G'), 66 ('B') does not occur at any even index of rings, then the function returns a result r and r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(rings)/2. The byte slice rings has length 2*n for some integer n with 1 <= n <= 100. For every j with 0 <= j < n, rings[2*j] is one of the ASCII bytes 82 ('R'), 71 ('G'), 66 ('B'), and rings[2*j+1] is one of the ASCII bytes 48 ('0') through 57 ('9').

statement: Let U be the number of distinct rod labels d in {0,1,...,9} that occur in rings, i.e. for which there exists j with 0 <= j < n and rings[2*j+1] = 48+d. If every such occurring rod label d is complete in rings (meaning 82, 71, and 66 each occur on rod d), then the function returns a result r and r = U.
preconditions: Let n = len(rings)/2. The byte slice rings has length 2*n for some integer n with 1 <= n <= 100. For every j with 0 <= j < n, rings[2*j] is one of the ASCII bytes 82 ('R'), 71 ('G'), 66 ('B'), and rings[2*j+1] is one of the ASCII bytes 48 ('0') through 57 ('9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r > 0, there exists a rod label d in {0,1,...,9} such that d is complete in rings (i.e. 82, 71, and 66 each occur on rod d).
preconditions: Let n = len(rings)/2. The byte slice rings has length 2*n for some integer n with 1 <= n <= 100. For every j with 0 <= j < n, rings[2*j] is one of the ASCII bytes 82 ('R'), 71 ('G'), 66 ('B'), and rings[2*j+1] is one of the ASCII bytes 48 ('0') through 57 ('9').

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 10 if and only if every rod label d in {0,1,...,9} is complete in rings (i.e. for every d, each of 82, 71, and 66 occurs on rod d).
preconditions: Let n = len(rings)/2. The byte slice rings has length 2*n for some integer n with 1 <= n <= 100. For every j with 0 <= j < n, rings[2*j] is one of the ASCII bytes 82 ('R'), 71 ('G'), 66 ('B'), and rings[2*j+1] is one of the ASCII bytes 48 ('0') through 57 ('9').

statement: Assume that for every d in {0,1,...,9} and every color byte c in {82,71,66}, c occurs on rod d in rings1 (there exists j with 0 <= j < len(rings1)/2, rings1[2*j] = c, and rings1[2*j+1] = 48+d) if and only if c occurs on rod d in rings2 (with the analogous condition using rings2). Then whenever count_points(rings1) returns r1 and count_points(rings2) returns r2, r1 = r2.
preconditions: Both rings1 and rings2 satisfy the S1 preconditions: each has length twice an integer between 1 and 100, with color bytes at even indices and digit bytes at odd indices.

statement: The function does not fail on rings: it returns a result r (in Lean, the evaluation is Result.ok r for some 64-bit integer r).
preconditions: Let n = len(rings)/2. The byte slice rings has length 2*n for some integer n with 1 <= n <= 100. For every j with 0 <= j < n, rings[2*j] is one of the ASCII bytes 82 ('R'), 71 ('G'), 66 ('B'), and rings[2*j+1] is one of the ASCII bytes 48 ('0') through 57 ('9').

statement: When count_points(rings1) returns r1 and count_points(rings2) returns r2, we have r1 <= r2 <= r1 + 1.
preconditions: rings1 and rings2 both satisfy the S1 preconditions, with n1 = len(rings1)/2 and n2 = len(rings2)/2. Moreover, rings2 is obtained from rings1 by appending one color-position pair: n2 = n1 + 1, for every j with 0 <= j < n1 we have rings2[2*j] = rings1[2*j] and rings2[2*j+1] = rings1[2*j+1], and for some color byte c in {82,71,66} and digit d in {0,...,9} we have rings2[2*n1] = c and rings2[2*n1+1] = 48+d.
